ANSWER: Three of the five (course_env.gd, environment_builder.gd, v2_world.gd) are identical `(bearing, radius, y) -> Vector3` polar-to-Cartesian conversions; hero_world.gd shares that signature/return type but adds a `BEARING_SHIFT` offset inside the angle formula, and environment_stage.gd is distinct with a different `(centre_x, centre_z, bearing, radius) -> Vector2` signature that also offsets by a plan-position centre.
FILES: godot/assets/marble_machine/course/course_env.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_builder.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_stage.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/hero_world.gd, godot/assets/marble_machine/v2/v2_world.gd
SYMBOLS: _polar (godot/assets/marble_machine/course/course_env.gd:827-830), _polar (godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_builder.gd:51-53), _polar (godot/assets/marble_machine/environment/environment_stage.gd:101-109), _polar (godot/assets/marble_machine/hero/hero_world.gd:155-157), _polar (godot/assets/marble_machine/v2/v2_world.gd:131-133)
EVIDENCE: course_env.gd:827-830 body reads `static func _polar(bearing: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3: ... return Vector3(sin(angle)*radius, y, cos(angle)*radius)` with `angle := deg_to_rad(bearing)`; environment_builder.gd:51-53 has the identical signature, return type, and formula with no comment; environment_stage.gd:101-109 has signature `(centre_x: float, centre_z: float, bearing: float, radius: float) -> Vector2` returning `Vector2(centre_x + sin(angle)*radius, centre_z + cos(angle)*radius)`; hero_world.gd:155-157 has signature `(bearing_degrees: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3` but computes `angle := deg_to_rad(bearing_degrees + BEARING_SHIFT)` before the same `Vector3(sin*radius, y, cos*radius)` return, and hero_world.gd:152 shows `BEARING_SHIFT` is a module-level const (`VIEW_BEARING - AUTHORED_BEARING`) used inside the formula; v2_world.gd:131-133 has signature `(bearing_degrees: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3` with `angle := deg_to_rad(bearing_degrees)` and the same `Vector3(sin*radius, y, cos*radius)` return, matching course_env/environment_builder aside from the cosmetic `bearing_degrees` vs `bearing` parameter name.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
